Follow one workflow from checked input tables to figures you can explain: practise, explore supplied datasets, then analyse your own data.

::: {.callout-note}
### Choose how to begin

**New to the workflow?** [Set up your workspace](00-setup.qmd), then follow the synthetic practice in order. **Just exploring?** Read the figures first. **Bringing your own data?** Use the checklist for your own study after setup.
:::

You will work from prepared feature tables. Raw sequencing processing and statistical hypothesis testing are outside this guide's workflow.

## Practice with synthetic data

Begin with 24 synthetic samples and 15 fictional features. Learn to read composition and Shannon diversity plots, then check the figures against the saved tables. An optional exercise reproduces one sample's values.

[Begin the practice example](examples/community-comparison/00-start-here.qmd)

## Follow the DietSwap walkthrough

Use the supplied study tables to investigate composition and diversity. Check the participant and sampling information before deciding which comparison the data support.

[Follow the DietSwap walkthrough](examples/dietswap/00-start-here.qmd)

## Apply the workflow to Mouse59

Explore 59 samples and 2,027 OTUs in two supplied groups. Compare OTU composition and diversity, investigate low-count samples, and verify your observations against the tables.

This demonstration uses OTU identifiers as labels because taxonomic assignments are unavailable.

[Follow the Mouse59 demonstration](examples/mouse59/00-start-here.qmd)

## Analyse your own study

Prepare your three tidy TSV files in `data/my-study/`, check the identifiers, and apply the same workflow. Verify the results and write a conclusion supported by your evidence.

[Prepare your own analysis](examples/my-study/00-start-here.qmd)

Use [Run the workflow](01-run-the-workflow.qmd) whenever a page asks you to generate or refresh outputs.
